findingDetails.title: The lookup offer interpolates the runtime label into a model-pasted shell command unquoted
findingDetails.case: an adapter or transport passes a runtime label carrying a space, semicolon or $(): the section writes it into the command the receiving model is told to run, so the label becomes shell syntax
findingDetails.scopeProof: buildHistoryLookupBody is the only site rendering a runtime label into shell text; the other two interpolated values pass through shellQuote (lookup-offer.ts:52-54,70); no in-tree producer sends an unsafe label
findingDetails.claim: The offer runtime label is the one interpolated value that is neither quoted nor whitelisted, so an unsafe label becomes shell syntax in the receiving session.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked every in-tree producer reachable from this module: cli.ts:510-512 admits only pi|devin|dsh|opencode|vibe and detectHistoryRuntime returns claude|codex|null; compaction adapters pass literals. No caller sends an attacker-shaped label today.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The label could be treated as a closed vocabulary owned by the type system; it is not, because the type is a plain string and the read-side enum runs only after state is read.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A producer is shown to pass a runtime label derived from an environment variable or event field without a whitelist, which would raise this to P1.

noveltyJustification: One new P2 from a previously uncovered dimension; no prior finding re-raised; the operator residuals were dispositioned as carried or exhausted rather than rediscovered.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: A trust-boundary review over a multi-runtime CLI, a locator schema, and a model-visible command surface; 63 declared files.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Every module on the executable trust path from argv to a rendered reply, plus the contract that specifies the injection.
omittedHighRiskTargets: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers source (outside the declared target; only its README and test are in scope)

searchLedger.hypothesis: A value interpolated into the model-pasted shell command can escape its argument.

searchActions.result: sessionId and handle are quoted; runtime label is raw

searchLedger.rationale: The one unquoted interpolation is the runtime label, which is typed string and not whitelisted at render time.

searchLedger.hypothesis: An argv session id reaches the state-file path before schema validation.

searchActions.result: sessionId is SHA-256 hashed to 16 hex chars before join

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: the id is hashed into the filename, so no separator or parent segment survives

searchLedger.hypothesis: Runtime, workspace or locator kind can be spoofed to read another store.

searchActions.result: enum agreement, realpath equality, strict-inside sessionDirectory, and ambiguity refusal all hold

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: every gate is checked before a store is read and ambiguity refuses rather than ranks

searchLedger.hypothesis: Private reasoning or store paths leak into a reply or a refusal.

searchActions.result: thinking/signature/redacted are projected out; refusals carry a code only

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: the public projection drops private blocks and every refusal prints only {ok:false,code}

searchLedger.hypothesis: The handle is an authorization token whose comparison or TTL can be bypassed.

searchActions.result: digest is identity-bound, not secret; mintedAt is outside it but the state file is 0700 and same-user

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: the handle is not a privilege boundary and the actor able to rewrite state already reads the store directly

searchLedger.hypothesis: Search allocates per-transcript content without a size gate.

searchActions.result: eager index over every item on first search; no workload measured

searchLedger.deferredReason: read-only pass cannot measure peak memory; carried as a D4 candidate with a required measurement
searchLedger.rationale: Real shape, unmeasured impact; not raised as a finding to avoid an unmeasured performance claim.

title: The lookup offer interpolates the runtime label into a model-pasted shell command unquoted

detail: Security trust boundary: no new P0/P1. One latent P2 (unquoted runtime label). Five directions ruled out, one deferred (pages.ts input bounds, unmeasured search memory).

evidence: .skilled/hooks/injection-contract.md:236 vs lookup-offer.ts:68-76 (no transcript text, data-not-instructions line at 74)
carried from iteration 1; parent spec.md:102 names the old path
no checklist/acceptance-criteria in target; deferred to D3

direction: path traversal through the argv session id
reason: getStatePath hashes the id before joining the state dir (cli.ts:187-190, hook-state.ts:484-487)

direction: prompt injection from retrieved content into a command
reason: content is JSON-serialized and sliced; offer carries no transcript text and states the data rule

direction: handle timing or replay as an auth boundary
reason: digest is not a bearer secret; holder already reads the store
state file is 0700 and same-user; no privilege crossing

direction: world-readable hook state in the OS temp dir

reason: both copies quote identically and bound the quoted form (hook-state.ts:281-284, lookup-offer.ts:52-59)
navigator re-validates each id as a string of at most 128 characters
